evals.name: answer-only-query-writes-no-log-entry
evals.description: Populated wiki at CWD; user asks a question answerable from one existing page and the prompt directs the agent to work the <query> workflow step by step, carrying no filing instruction of its own. The skill's own filing rule must produce the skip: no page under queries/, summaries/, or comparisons/, no log.md entry (log.md stays byte-identical to its staged state), and a one-line filing decision whose reason names the filing rule's own trigger — the three-page count, or the cross-page reasoning/synthesis the answer lacks. That last assertion is the discriminating one, and its pattern deliberately excludes the superseded text's vocabulary: "skip trivial lookups" already produced a skip reported as a "trivial single-page lookup" in 4 of 5 baseline passes, so accepting bare single-page phrasing measured almost nothing, and "novel reasoning" is likewise the old step's own wording ("multi-source synthesis, structured comparison, novel reasoning") rather than the new rule's. Discriminates both the changes-only log rule and the deterministic filing default from their vaguer predecessors: pass rate is the measurement, so run >=5 passes per side when comparing skill revisions.

evals.name: reingest-unchanged-source-skips
evals.description: Re-ingest of an UNCHANGED source against a wiki that already carries the raw sidecar and its correct recorded sha256. The prompt asks for a plain re-ingest and names no comparison mode, so the hub's "Re-ingest compares before it writes" bullet has to supply the whole procedure: build a temp copy carrying the recorded sha256 over the fresh body, run compute_sha256.py --check on that copy while the sidecar stays untouched, read `ok`/exit 0 as unchanged, and skip. The outcome assertions are byte-identity of the sidecar and of log.md — the only way to prove "no hash rewrite", since the write mode would refresh the hash to the value it already holds and leave no trace. The discriminating assertions are the three procedure fields: the superseded instruction reran the default write mode over the sidecar itself, which reports `ok` here too and so produces the same filesystem outcome from the wrong comparison. Pass rate is the measurement; the fixed denominator is this file's top-level `passes`.

- `drift_check_command`: the exact command line you ran to decide whether the source changed, copied verbatim on one line. `n/a` only if you ran no such command.
- `drift_check_target`: `sidecar` if that command read the on-disk `raw/` sidecar, `temp-file` if it read a temporary copy outside the wiki tree, `n/a` if you ran no such command.

evals.name: reingest-changed-source-surfaces-drift
evals.description: Re-ingest of a CHANGED source: the sidecar records the release-2.0 body (BLUE) with a matching sha256, and the on-disk source now ships release 3.0 (CRIMSON). Same request and constraints as L2-8, so the fixture alone drives the branch and the pair proves the rule branches rather than always taking one side. The compare must report `update`/exit 1 from the temp copy while the sidecar is still untouched, and only then may the body be rewritten and the hash refreshed. raw_sha256_matches_body plus the absent old hash is what makes "the recorded hash changes only together with that body rewrite" checkable without predicting the agent's exact body bytes: a hash refreshed over an unrewritten body fails the CRIMSON check, and a body rewritten with a stale hash fails the self-consistency check. Pass rate is the measurement; the fixed denominator is this file's top-level `passes`.
